GIGAGPU RTX 4090 Llama 3.1 8B benchmark reports ~95 tok/s single-stream FP16 decode on vLLM 0.6.4 (PyTorch 2.5, CUDA 12.6), corroborated across multiple independent citations of that page. It is a memory-bandwidth ceiling (~16GB weights / 1008 GB/s). One caveat: the FP16 figure was measured with enforce_eager=true (torch.compile/CUDA graphs disabled), which if anything understates true FP16 single-stream; so 95 is a conservative floor, not an overstatement. Confirmed as a defensible single-stream FP16 number.

The ~190 tok/s (≈2x FP16) figure is well-grounded: decode is bandwidth-bound, halving weight bytes (16GB→8GB) roughly doubles the read rate, and Ada 4th-gen tensor cores accept FP8 natively. Naive ceilings: 1008/8=126 t/s FP8 vs 1008/16=63 t/s FP16; measured numbers exceed both via L2 caching, and the ~2x ratio shows up cleanly. Note the raw tensor-core compute speedup is lower (~1.45x per NVIDIA Transformer Engine), but for autoregressive single-stream decode the bandwidth-driven ~2x holds. Reasonable; medium confidence retained because it is a derived/rounded number, not a directly published single-stream FP8 measurement.

Level1Techs (lhl) results confirm Shisa V2 8B (Llama 3) Q4_K_M: Vulkan fa=1 tg128 = 42.0 t/s; HIP/ROCm = 37.2 t/s. Exact match. The ~48 t/s 'owner-reported best' is anecdotal/quant-dependent and should not be the planning figure; 42 t/s Vulkan is the defensible decode number. Tested on 128GB Framework Desktop, ~215 GB/s effective bandwidth.
Level1Techs (lhl) confirms Shisa V2 8B Q4_K_M prefill (pp512): HIP hipBLASLt = 878.2 t/s; Vulkan fa=1 = 614.2 t/s. Exact match.

Level1Techs (lhl) confirms Qwen3 30B-A3B UD-Q4_K_XL: Vulkan fa=1 tg128 = 66.3 t/s, pp512 = 604.8 t/s; Vulkan batch=256 tg128 = 72.0 t/s. Exact match. This is the standout Strix Halo LLM figure (MoE fits its bandwidth profile well).

Level1Techs (lhl) confirms Mistral Small 3.1 24B UD-Q4_K_XL: HIP hipBLASLt tg128 = 13.6 t/s, pp512 = 316.9 t/s. Exact match for the HIP decode figure cited. Minor context: Vulkan fa=1 is actually slightly faster on decode here (14.3 t/s) while much slower on prefill (119.6 t/s) — so 13.6 HIP is a valid but not the peak decode number.

Level1Techs (lhl) confirms Shisa V2 70B (Llama 3) Q4_K_M: Vulkan fa=1 tg128 = 5.0 t/s (pp512 26.4); HIP/ROCm rocWMMA tg128 = 4.5 t/s (pp512 94.7). Exact match. The 'owner-reported 12-15 t/s at heavier quant' is anecdotal and quant-dependent — 5 t/s at Q4_K_M is the defensible figure; do not plan on 12-15.

Qualitative claim supported by the Level1Techs data itself: HIP/ROCm wins prefill on dense models (e.g. 24B 316.9 vs 119.6; 70B 94.7 vs 26.4) while Vulkan often wins/ties decode (8B 42.0 vs 37.2; 70B 5.0 vs 4.5). The 'Vulkan degrades past ~4K ctx, ROCm+FA stays flat past 8K' claim is consistent with the kyuz0 amd-strix-halo-toolboxes writeups. Directionally sound; treat as guidance, not a precise number.

LMSYS review and NVIDIA specs confirm GB10: up to 273 GB/s LPDDR5x unified bandwidth, 128 GB coherent unified memory. Exact match. This is the decode bottleneck (bandwidth/model-size = ceiling token rate).

AMD spec: 256-bit LPDDR5x-8000 interface -> 8000 MT/s x 256 bit / 8 = ~256 GB/s theoretical peak, 128 GB unified. Confirmed. Important for a decode-throughput model: real-world measured is only ~212-215 GB/s under mixed CPU+GPU load (~16% below theoretical), which is why Strix Halo decode sits slightly below its 256 GB/s implies — and slightly below DGX Spark's 273 GB/s in practice.

checked.note: Confirmed despite the finder's conf-low flag: the ReQAT paper reports NVFP4 achieves up to 3.93x output-token throughput over BF16 on DGX Spark via trtllm-bench (1K requests, 512-token prompts, batching up to 256, 8K max gen). Do not apply 3.93x to single-stream decode.

The ~125 TFLOPS BF16/FP16 dense figure is NOT officially published by NVIDIA and is disputed. NVIDIA officially states only 1 PFLOP FP4 and 31 TFLOPS FP32. The 125 TF number is a community derivation (assuming a 1:8 dense-BF16-to-sparse-FP4 ratio); critics note RTX Blackwell parts use a 1:16 ratio, which would imply ~62 TF dense BF16. John Carmack's real-world measurement was ~60 TFLOPS BF16, and one independent bench repo saw only ~11-12 TFLOPS. Finder's own 'conf low' and 'derived, not officially published' caveats are correct; treat 125 as an unverified upper estimate, ~60 as measured.
